This page lists some of the datasets we will use in this course. You can add datasets you find to this page by clicking "Edit this page" at the bottom and submitting a pull request.

## National Medical Expenditure Study

Results from the 1987 National Medical Expenditure Study

```{r, eval=FALSE}
data(nmes, package = 'TriMatch')
```

## Effects of tutoring services on course grades

Results from a study examining the effects of tutoring services on course grades. This is the dataset that inspired the [`TriMatch`](https://github.com/jbryer/TriMatch) package for making matched triplets (i.e. three groups, two treatments, one control).

```{r, eval=FALSE}
data(tutoring, package = 'TriMatch')
```

## The Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study (TIMSS) 

[The Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study](https://www.iea.nl/studies/iea/timss) (TIMSS) provides reliable and timely trend data on the mathematics and science achievement of U.S. students compared to that of students in other countries. TIMSS data have been collected from students at grades 4 and 8 every 4 years since 1995, with the United States participating in every administration of TIMSS. TIMSS Advanced studies the achievement in advanced mathematics and physics of students in their final year of secondary school. It has been conducted in 1995, 2008, and 2015, with the United States participating in 1995 and 2015. TIMSS and TIMSS Advanced are sponsored by the International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement (IEA) and conducted in the United States by the National Center for Education Statistics (NCES).

```{r, eval=FALSE}
EdSurvey::downloadTIMSS(root = "data/", years = c(2019), cache = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)
timss <- EdSurvey::readTIMSS(path = 'data/TIMSS/2019/', countries = 'USA', gradeLvl = '8')
```


## Effects of bed nets

```{r, eval=FALSE}
bed_nets <- read.csv('https://evalsp21.classes.andrewheiss.com/data/bed_nets_observed.csv')
```

## `causaldata` R package

The [`causaldata`](https://github.com/nickch-k/causaldata) R package contains a number of datasets from the books [*The Effect*](https://theeffectbook.net/), [*Causal Inference: The Mixtape*](https://mixtape.scunning.com/index.html), and [*Causal Inference: What If?*](https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/miguel-hernan/causal-inference-book/).

```{r}
causaldata_tables <- data(package = 'causaldata')
knitr::kable(causaldata_tables$results[,c('Item', 'Title')], row.names = FALSE)
```

## `ForCausality` R package

Provides a comprehensive set of datasets and tools for 'causal inference' research. The package includes data from clinical trials, cancer studies, epidemiological surveys, environmental exposures, and health-related observational studies. Designed to facilitate causal analysis, risk assessment, and advanced statistical modeling, it leverages datasets from packages such as 'causalOT', 'survival', 'causalPAF', 'evident', 'melt', and 'sanon'. 

```{r}
ForCausality_tables <- data(package = 'ForCausality')
knitr::kable(ForCausality_tables$results[,c('Item', 'Title')], row.names = FALSE)
```

## Gerber and Green Dataset used by Imai

This is a classic dataset used to show propensity score analysis, however if you read the following articles you will see there is much debate about the analyses conducted by Gerber and Donald as well as Imai.

Gerber A.S. & Donald, P.G. (2000). The effects of personal canvassing, telephone calls, and direct mail on voter turnout: A field experiment. *American Political Science Review, 94*(3), 653– 64.

Imai, K. (2005). Do get-out-the-vote calls reduce turnout? The importance of statistical methods for field experiments. *American Political Science Review, 99*(2), 283– 300.

Gerber, A.S. & Donald P.G. (2005). Correction to Gerber and Green (2000), replication of disputed findings, and reply to Imai (2005). *American Political Science Review, 99*(2), 301-13.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
data(GerberGreenImai, package = 'Matching')
```

## Linked Birth/Infant Death Cohort Data

Data on twins from the [National Bureau of Economic Research](https://www.nber.org/research/data/linked-birthinfant-death-cohort-data). These data are based on this paper:

Almond, D., Chay, K.Y, & Lee, D.S. (2005). The costs of low birth weight. *The Quarterly Journal of Economics, 120*(3), 1031-1083.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
data(twins, package = 'psa')
```


## Programme of International Student Assessment (PISA)

[PISA](https://www.oecd.org/en/about/programmes/pisa.html) is the OECD's Programme for International Student Assessment. PISA measures 15-year-olds’ ability to use their reading, mathematics and science knowledge and skills to meet real-life challenges.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Years available using the EdSurvey package: 2000 2003 2006 2009 2012 2015 2018
EdSurvey::downloadPISA(years = 2018, database = "INT", root = "data/")
pisa2018 <- EdSurvey::readPISA(path = "data/PISA/2018", countries = "USA")
```

The `EdSurvey` package only goes to 2018. Data for [2022](https://webfs.oecd.org/pisa2022/index.html#section1) and [2025](https://webfs.oecd.org/pisa2022/index.html#section0) are available on the [OEC website](https://www.oecd.org/en/about/programmes/pisa.html).

```{r, eval=FALSE}
path <- 'data/PISA/'

#' Download zip files from urls
download_zip_files <- function(urls, dest, keep_zip = FALSE) {
	dir.create(dest, recursive = TRUE)
	for(i in urls) {
		dest_file <- file.path(dest, basename(i))
		download.file(i, dest_file)
		unzip(dest_file, exdir = dest)
		if(!keep_zip) {
			unlink(dest_file)
		}
	}
}

# 2025 PISA
download_zip_files(
	urls = c(
		'https://webfs.oecd.org/pisa2022/2025/CY09_MS_SCH_PUF.zip',
		'https://webfs.oecd.org/pisa2022/2025/CY09_MS_STU_PUF.zip',
		'https://webfs.oecd.org/pisa2022/2025/CY09_MS_TCH_PUF.zip'
		# Optional other files
		# 'https://webfs.oecd.org/pisa2022/2025/CY09_MS_COG_PUF.zip',
		# 'https://webfs.oecd.org/pisa2022/2025/CY09_MS_COG_PROCESS_PUF.zip'
	),
	dest = file.path(path, '2025')
)
# You will have to load and merge the data frames manually
pisa2025_student <- haven::read_sav(file.path(path, '2025', 'CY09_MS_SCH_PUF.SAV'))
pisa2025_school <- haven::read_sav(file.path(path, '2025', 'CY09_MS_SCH_PUF.SAV'))
pisa2025_teacher <- haven::read_sav(file.path(path, '2025', 'CY09_MS_TCH_PUF.sav'))
save(pisa2025_student, pisa2025_school, pisa2025_teacher, file = 'data/pisa2025.rda') # You can use load() to read it back in

# 2022 PISA
download_zip_files(
	urls = c(
		'https://webfs.oecd.org/pisa2022/SCH_QQQ_SPSS.zip',
		'https://webfs.oecd.org/pisa2022/STU_QQQ_SPSS.zip',
		'https://webfs.oecd.org/pisa2022/TCH_QQQ_SPSS.zip'
		# Optional other files
		# 'https://webfs.oecd.org/pisa2022/STU_COG_SPSS.zip',
		# 'https://webfs.oecd.org/pisa2022/STU_TIM_SPSS.zip',
		# 'https://webfs.oecd.org/pisa2022/CRT_SPSS.zip',
		# 'https://webfs.oecd.org/pisa2022/FLT_SPSS.zip',
		# 'https://webfs.oecd.org/pisa2022/escs_trend.zip'
	),
	dest = file.path(path, '2022')
)
pisa2022_student <- haven::read_sav(file.path(path, '2022', 'CY08MSP_STU_QQQ.SAV'))
pisa2022_school <- haven::read_sav(file.path(path, '2022', 'CY08MSP_SCH_QQQ.SAV'))
pisa2022_teacher <- haven::read_sav(file.path(path, '2022', 'CY08MSP_TCH_QQQ.SAV'))
save(pisa2022_student, pisa2022_school, pisa2022_teacher, file = 'data/pisa2022.rda') # You can use load() to read it back in
```
